semantics.note: The business-copy scope and the categorical 'always' are kept. 'Questionable' softens the conclusion, but 'always require enough editing' is a firm factual assertion.

contract.note: Reading the claim as a test of total task time including editing, at comparable quality, on ordinary business writing in 2023 to the post date is fair. The contract notes the gap between experimental tasks and production work.

evidence.note: A peer-reviewed randomized trial (July 2023) of professional writing tasks: total time fell 40% and quality rose 18%.
The original working paper: 68% of treated participants submitted ChatGPT output unedited, and editing added no measured quality. This contradicts 'always require enough editing'.
The institution's summary lists limitations: no fact-checking and no company-specific context. Real-world savings may be smaller, but the article does not show that they vanish.

reviews.rationale: A contemporaneous randomized study on professional business-writing tasks found large total time savings at higher quality. Most participants submitted outputs without editing. That defeats the claim that outputs 'always' need enough editing to make the time savings questionable. Real-world limits on fact-checking temper the effect size but do not restore the blanket claim.
